notes:
Customer: large retail trading platform; highly sensitive PII + trade data. 
Key ask: predictable throughput during US market open (09:30-16:00 ET) with cross-AZ failover and sub-75ms p95 for routing/rerank calls.
Quotes from infra lead: "We cannot have model degradation during market peaks — need hard headroom guarantees, not best-effort."
They prefer model pinning + automatic fallback to quantized variant if warm pool exhausted.
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to 12mo reserved if SLA on throughput and incident MTTR included.
Requested artifacts: capacity plan, per-AZ failover runbook, SLO appendix for contract, stub pricing for 3 sizing bands.
use_case_summary:
Primary workloads: live customer-chat assistant (context windows 2k-4k), high-frequency reranking for recommendation pipeline, nightly embeddings for risk analytics.
Latency & throughput targets: target p95 <= 75ms for rerank endpoints at steady state; target sustained throughput 1200 tokens/sec per region for peak windows; concurrency target 450 simultaneous chat sessions with KV-cache hit expected at 60%.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — favors predictable reserved pricing over on-demand spikes.
reserved_gpu_plan:
Initial sizing proposal v1: total reserved = 24 standard A100-equivalent GPUs across 2 regions (us-east-1, us-west-2) distributed as 14 GPUs primary region (us-east-1) + 10 GPUs secondary (us-west-2).
Failover headroom: target 40% cross-region headroom (plan expects to re-route up to 40% of primary load to secondary within 60s).
AZ distribution: within region, recommend 3 AZs with at least N+1 redundancy; suggested pool per AZ = at least 4 GPUs in primary region.
Autoscaling & burst: 20% burst buffer via shared burst pool for seasonal spikes (billed at premium) + automatic fallback to quantized model variant to reduce memory and GPU per-token cost by ~30%.
Rationales: preserves market-open latency SLOs, keeps warm KV-cache residency for top 25% of sessions, and provides deterministic failover behaviour required by compliance.
sla_negotiation_points:
- p95 latency SLO: customer requests 75ms p95 for rerank & 120ms p95 for chat during peak windows; Redwood to provide metrics, penalties tied to sustained breach >15min.
- Throughput guarantee: 1.2k tokens/sec sustained per region during peak; Redwood requested a 10% tolerance band.
- MTTR: 30 min for infra incidents (failover to secondary region) requested by customer; Redwood proposed 60 min with automated routing checks.
- Data residency: primary data to remain in customer VPC; audit logs retained 12 months (customer prefers 24 months).
- Pricing: customer asks for tiered discounts at 12mo commit with elasticity for 6mo burst credits.
Negotiation status: early — legal reviewing SLA appendix, security wants detailed KMS and network diagrams.
